subject: Renewal discussion — commit sizing, cost credits, and perf ROI
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Beckett <sam.beckett@tidalai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 15:08:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal touch — usage snapshot + early options

Hi Sam,

We’ve pulled a short usage snapshot ahead of your Q3 renewal to surface a couple of operational opportunities. High-level: your token spend has grown 38% QoQ driven by a 2x increase in streaming chat throughput for customer support; latency-sensitive inference (user-facing completion) accounts for ~65% of total tokens.

Attached is a short PDF with per-route cost breakdown and a first-pass ROI calc (tidal_usage_Q2_report.pdf). Before we schedule a renewal call, two quick asks so we come prepared:
- Can you confirm the expected headcount/usage growth for the next 6 months (percent or rough numbers)?
- Are you prioritizing latency (95th pct <200ms) or cost/unit efficiency for the next term?

I’ll propose a couple of commit/credit shapes based on your answers and the current performance profile — we can bend terms (headroom corridors, burst credits) to match traffic seasonality.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.l@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: tidal_usage_Q2_report.pdf (summary, 3 pages)
From: Sam Beckett <sam.beckett@tidalai.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 18:13:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal touch — usage snapshot + early options

Thanks Jasmine — useful start. Quick answers:
- Growth: expect ~50% net token growth over next 6 months as we roll chat to two more regions and increase model depth for recommendations.
- Priority: latency is still a blocker for product adoption; we’d accept a modest increase in unit cost if it guarantees <200ms 95th for frontend requests.

Two follow-ups: can you show what a 12-month commit with burst credits looks like vs a 6-month flexible term? Also curious how much we’d save if we shift 30% of non-latency traffic to cheaper embeddings/quantized variants.

Sam
Sam Beckett
Head of Platform, Tidal AI
sam.beckett@tidalai.com
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 10:02:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Renewal touch — usage snapshot + early options

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Sam’s answers. He called out 50% growth and latency priority. Can you help:
1) A recommended commit vs 6-month flexible layout with projected unit economics (tokens/month, effective $/1M tokens) and where burst credits apply.
2) A short ops runbook we can send Sam that describes how to route non-latency traffic to cheaper variants + expected cost delta.

I attached the usage PDF we sent earlier. If you can draft a 1-page playbook (or point me to an existing template) I’ll send to Sam and propose a 30-min renewal alignment next week.

Thanks — Jasmine

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.l@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 14:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal touch — usage snapshot + early options

Got it. Drafting numbers below (initials for internal review) — I’ll attach a short spreadsheet (commit_playbook_v1.xlsx) with modeled scenarios.

Summary (baseline = current run-rate):
- Current tokens/month: ~1.1B tokens. Projected 6-month run-rate w/ 50% growth = ~1.65B tokens/month.
- 6-month flexible term (no commit): unit price stays at current hosted rate; no burst credits; effective $/1M = $X (see sheet).
- 12-month commit (staged): 20% uplift in committed tokens relative to current run-rate (commit = 1.32B tokens/month) + 25% burst credits available for spikes. Effective $/1M drops by ~18% vs flexible.
- Option B: 12-month corridor commit (1.0B guaranteed, headroom upto 1.8B with graduated pricing) — recommended if they want predictability but need headroom.

Latency/Perf path:
- Keep high-priority frontend on lowest-latency variants (dedicated pool) — modeled cost increase ~12% but meets <200ms 95th.
- Migrate 30% of worker traffic (batch re-ranks, embedding prep) to quantized variants / cheaper families — modeled savings ~22% on that slice.

Next steps I recommend we send Sam: 1) 1-page commit playbook (attached), 2) 2-row pricing comparison (6mo flex vs 12mo commit + corridor), 3) proposed cadence: 30-min call + DocuSign for a 12-month staged commit with a 30-day evaluation window.

I’ve attached commit_playbook_v1.xlsx and a short exporter that trims the econ rows for sales decks.

-Ben
Director, Customer Success Operations
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Renewal alignment + proposed next steps

Sam — thanks for the quick answers and for confirming the growth target. Attached is a short 2-page playbook (commit_playbook_v1.xlsx exported as PDF in the follow-up) that summarizes the options we discussed:
- 6-month flexible (no commit): most operational flexibility, higher unit price, no burst credits.
- 12-month staged commit (recommended): 20% committed uplift + 25% burst credits; estimated unit savings ~18% and delivers <200ms 95th on dedicated pool for frontend.
- Corridor commit (recommended if they need headroom): guarantees a floor + graduated pricing bands up to 1.8B tokens.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-min alignment call next Tue 04/06 or Wed 04/07 — I can cover pricing, Ben will cover the playbook, Monica will sketch the migration steps.
2) If we agree on 12-month staged commit, we’ll send a DocuSign term sheet with a 30-day evaluation period.
3) Pre-sign: Ben’s team will share a short ops checklist for shifting batch traffic to quantized variants (expected ~22% savings on that slice).
